names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Νοεμβρίου, «Όσιος Μαρτίνος ο θαυματουργός επίσκοπος Φραγκιάς», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 12. октобар ст. ст., „Св. Мартин еп. Турски.“ — Св. is «saint» and not a rank and еп. Турски is the `bishop` this corpus puts in `types` with the see in `office`, so all of it comes off and the bare personal name is the whole of the form. `foldchk.py` measured the string as held by `martin-of-illyria` and `martin-pope-of-rome` before this day, both `sr`, so this form makes a three-folder fold, read in the `serbian` row’s note and in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs`.

birth.note: days.pravoslavie.ru's life opens «Святитель Мартин Милостивый, епископ Турский, (316–397) родился в начале IV века в Паннонии». saint.gr gives no year of birth at all: «Ο Όσιος Μαρτίνος έζησε τον 4ο αιώνα μ.Χ. και καταγόταν από τη Σαβωρία της Παννονίας», and has him die aged eighty-one.

death.note: One page disagreeing with itself is read exactly as two churches disagreeing are, and days.pravoslavie.ru disagrees with itself here. Its life heads him «(316–397)» and says two thousand monks came to his funeral «в 397 году»; its own day line for 12 October prints «Свт. Мартина Милостивого, еп. Турского (ок. 400)». Nothing chooses between them, so the interval carries both. saint.gr gives no year and a second account two centuries off this one, recorded in the Greek row.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 октября ст. ст. — «Свт. Мартина Милостивого, еп. Турского (ок. 400).»
source.note: No rank is read onto this line. The day prints two icons and both are the plain service, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком» — a service the Typikon marks with no sign at all; each stands immediately before one great line of the first paragraph — the Tarsus martyrs, and Cosmas of Maiuma — and neither reaches a later line.

attestations.note: The Russian keeps him a month before the Greek does — 12 October against 12 November — and tells the Western life rather than the synaxaristic one: Pannonia and a non-Christian father who insisted on the army, the cloak divided in winter, Ligugé near Poitiers and then Marmoutier with its Egyptian rule, the see of Tours taken by a ruse, the death at Candes above the meeting of the Vienne and the Loire and the body carried off upriver by the people of Tours. It names Sulpicius Severus as his contemporary biographer, and it gives him the two years the Greek page lacks, before contradicting the second of them on its own day line.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Νοεμβρίου — «Όσιος Μαρτίνος ο θαυματουργός επίσκοπος Φραγκιάς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page sets two accounts of him side by side and says so: the first is the soldier of Sabaria in Pannonia who divided his cloak at Amiens and became bishop of Tours in the fourth century, and the second, «Άλλη συναξαριστική πηγή όμως, έχει διαφορετικό το βιογραφικό του σημείωμα», makes him a count and general under Trajan who became a monk and then bishop of a city of Gaul it calls Konstantinos. The life written here follows the page's first account and quotes the second as the page's own. The same day's calendar keeps a second Martin, the bishop of Tarakine, in a separate entry; that page says only that he is not the Martin of 10 November, and joins neither of them to this one, although both are called men of Sabaria in Pannonia. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.10.2026 (12. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. Мартин еп. Турски.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. The heading is quoted whole, with the closing full stop the Prologue itself prints, which is what BRIEF-SERBIAN section 4 asks for. It had to be measured off the raw cached page, because srbody.mjs and sr-cand.mjs both strip it from their printed output: every heading of this day ends ". " in the source. **THIS FOLDER HAD NO ROMANIAN AND NO SERBIAN ROW AND TWO NAME FORMS BETWEEN THREE BOOKS**, and the Greek keeps him on 11 October where the Russian and this book keep him on the 12th; this row is the Julian 12 October, the day this page prints him on. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND THE FIRST ITEM IS A PLACE NO OTHER BOOK READ FOR THIS FOLDER GIVES. He was born **in Pannonia, in a town of Styria**, in 316, of heathen parents, and his father was a Roman officer, which is how the boy came to be put into the army against his will. He was already a catechumen — «оглашен» — in the Church, which he had loved with his whole heart from early childhood. The cloak at the gate of Amiens is told in full: a beggar all but naked shivering in the frost, Martin falling behind his companions, the soldier's cloak cut in two with his sword, half given and half worn away. And the dream that night is given its words: Christ appeared wrapped in that half of the cloak and said to his angels, «Мартин је тек оглашен, и ево обуче ме својом одећом!» — Martin is only a catechumen, and see, he has clothed me with his own garment. THE REST: he left the army, was baptised at once, **and baptised his mother**; he became a monk in the diocese of Saint Hilary, at Poitiers; he was extraordinarily humble, and for that humility God gave him an abundant gift of wonderworking, so that he even raised the dead and drove out evil spirits; he was made bishop at Tours **against his will**; and after much labour and a hard struggle with heathen and with Arian heretics he gave up his soul in 397. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND BOTH ENDS CORROBORATED. The folder holds `birth` 316 and `death` «397 or about 400»; this entry gives 316 and 397 flat, which is the birth exactly and the earlier end of the death interval. **Narrowing a range to one end of itself on a second book's flat figure is refused**, so the death field is untouched and the agreement is recorded here. `types` UNTOUCHED at `bishop`, `wonderworker`: еп. in the heading is the `bishop`, «обилати дар чудотворства» corroborates the `wonderworker`, and **«замонаши» is a verb in the body and no warrant for a rank** — the heading has no Преп. `office` left at «Bishop of Tours»; the heading's «еп. Турски» and the body's «епископа у граду Гуру» both say it and neither improves it. `related` UNTOUCHED, AND THE ONE NAME IN THE ENTRY IS KEPT OUT OF THE PROSE ON SECTION 6'S GROUND. The entry says he was tonsured «у епархији св. Иларија Поатијског», in the diocese of Saint Hilary of Poitiers, and `hilary-of-poitiers` is that display name exactly — so writing the phrase whole would make `related-floor.test.mjs` demand a row in both directions, and **a diocese is a jurisdiction and not a companion**, the same reading that kept Sabbas the Sanctified's monastery out of Theophanes's prose on the Julian 11 October. The prose names only Saint Hilary, at Poitiers, which matches no display name; the book's own words are here. The beggar, the mother and the father take no rows. No `locations` — «у једноме граду Штајерске», in some town of Styria, is not a coordinate. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.
